settings.scrapyards.locations.laptopMode: Which prop the screen is drawn on. Only models this script knows the screen texture for can be used, which is why this is a list rather than a box.
settings.scrapyards.locations.laptop.des: Where the laptop sits. Place one where you want it, or point at one the yard already has — whichever button you use is what the yard then does.
settings.interact.laptopKeys.label: Keys usable at the laptop
settings.interact.laptopKeys.description: Sitting at a yard laptop switches every game control off, so a keybind cannot fire while you are typing into it — which also stops Escape reaching the pause menu. Anything listed here stays live anyway. Push-to-talk is always kept whether it is listed or not.
settings.basic.partsMode.label: Part fitment
settings.basic.partsMode.description: Per model: a part is for a particular car, bought for that car and refused on any other. Simple: every part fits everything.
settings.vehicleParts.price.label: Price
settings.vehicleParts.price.description: List price before any trade discount. Zero means the yards do not sell it.
settings.vehicleParts.condition.label: Condition
settings.vehicleParts.condition.descript: What grade the yards stock this at. Sets the price band and the odds it turns out to be dud.
settings.vehicleParts.leadHours.label: Lead time
settings.vehicleParts.leadHours.descript: How long it takes to come in, in real hours. Rolled once when you order. Zero to zero is on the shelf.
settings.vehicleParts.universal.label: Fits anything
settings.vehicleParts.universal.descript: Oil, coolant, paint, a battery. Ticked on the exceptions — everything else is already car-specific.
settings.vehicleParts.specificModels.des: Off is normal: the part is for whichever car you are looking at. On, it is only the models listed.
settings.vehicleParts.fitsModels.label: Models
settings.vehicleParts.fitsModels.descrip: The only cars this one fits. Picked from the Vehicles list.
settings.vehicleParts.needsTier.label: Needs tier
settings.vehicleParts.needsTier.descript: Rep gate. Below this tier the part is listed and priced but cannot be bought. Empty means anyone can.
settings.vehicleParts.revealAt.label: A dud one shows
settings.vehicleParts.revealAt.descripti: Panels, glass and paint you can see as they go on. An engine or a wheel gives nothing away until the car first runs.
settings.scrapyards.tiers.discount.label: Trade discount
settings.scrapyards.tiers.discount.descr: Taken off every list price at this tier, and totalled on the order as a saving.
settings.scrapyards.tiers.leadMultiplier: Scales every wait at this tier. Being served first is what a regular actually notices.
settings.scrapyards.dudChance.label: Odds a cheap part is dud
settings.scrapyards.dudChance.descriptio: How often a part turns out to be no good, by the grade it was sold at. It shows itself when you would find out in a workshop.
settings.scrapyards.dudChance.used.label: Used
settings.scrapyards.dudChance.oe.label: New / OE
settings.scrapyards.modelPriceFactor.des: A car-specific part costs its own price plus this much of what the car is worth, so a supercar's engine is dear and a Blista's is not.
settings.scrapyards.offSpecialityLead.de: A yard that does not deal in that sort of car will still send off for the part — it just takes this much longer.
settings.scrapyards.offSpecialitySurchar: And this much extra on top, for the trouble.
settings.blueprints.vehicles.price.label: Car value
settings.blueprints.vehicles.price.descr: What this car is worth. Car-specific parts are priced off it. Filled in from the framework where it knows the model, typed where it does not — what you type wins.
settings.vehicleParts.category.label: Shelf
settings.vehicleParts.category.descripti: Which shelf it sits on in the catalogue — the rail down the left of the laptop.
